title: First-Year Undergraduate Admission (USC)
text:
Note: this page covers fall 2027 entry (deadlines run from November 2026 through January 2027).

APPLICATION DEADLINES
- Early Decision (most majors): November 1. ED is binding. Performing arts programs do not participate.
- Early Action (most majors): November 1. EA is non-binding and non-restrictive. Performing arts programs do not participate.
- Regular Decision (performing arts majors): December 1. This covers the Kaufman School of Dance, School of Dramatic Arts, and Thornton School of Music.
- Regular Decision (most majors): apply by January 10, 2027.
- World Bachelor in Business (Marshall): must apply by the November 1 ED/EA deadline. WBB no longer participates in Regular Decision.

FINANCIAL AID DEADLINES (as listed on this page)
- Early Decision: November 1, 2026
- Early Action: November 15, 2026
- Regular Decision: February 3, 2027
- Cal Grant (California residents): March 2, 2027
- Need-based aid requires the FAFSA and CSS Profile. Undocumented or DACA students should submit their 2025 tax return instead of the FAFSA.

NOTIFICATION DATES
- ED: mid-December.
- EA: late January.
- Regular Decision (both December 1 and January 10 rounds): by April 1.

APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS
- Common Application: required. A fee waiver is available through the Common Application's Profile section if the fee is a financial burden.
- Test policy: test-optional. If submitted, USC uses the highest score in each SAT and ACT section. USC does not accept self-reported scores. SAT school code: 4852. ACT school code: 0470.
- Transcripts: official transcripts of all high school and college coursework completed.
- Letter of recommendation: one required, from a school counselor or teacher. Some programs may require more.
- Mid-year grades: submit fall grades using the Mid-Year Report form in the Common Application or through the applicant portal.
- Affirmations: completed in the applicant portal. A digital signature may be submitted after the deadline.
- International applicants: submit a Financial Statement of Personal or Family Support and, if applicable, English-proficiency exam scores.
- Home-schooled applicants: answer the home-school questions in the Common Application Secondary School Report. USC recommends externally graded work, such as SAT/ACT, AP, or accredited college or online coursework.

PORTFOLIOS, AUDITIONS, AND SUPPLEMENTS
- Some majors require a portfolio, resume, writing samples, or auditions.
- Schools with additional requirements: Iovine and Young Academy; School of Architecture; Roski School of Art and Design; School of Cinematic Arts; Kaufman School of Dance; School of Dramatic Arts; Thornton School of Music; Marshall School of Business (WBB).
- Some schools may also conduct interviews as part of their additional requirements.

OTHER POLICIES
- The Office of Undergraduate Admission does not conduct admission interviews or track demonstrated interest.
- Extensions for application deadlines are considered case by case. Contact your admission counselor to request one.

CONTACTS

- Location: University Park Campus
